title: Drafting a literature review section
prompt: A PhD student is drafting the literature review section of their dissertation. They use ChatGPT to generate an initial structured outline of key themes in their field, which they then refine, expand, and contextualize with their own critical analysis.

title: Drafting a literature review section (with disclosure in methods)
prompt: A PhD student is drafting the literature review section of their dissertation. They use ChatGPT to generate an initial structured outline of key themes in their field, which they then refine, expand, and contextualize with their own critical analysis. They plan to disclose in the methodology section that an AI tool was used to structure themes.

title: Drafting a literature review section (advisor approves AI use)
prompt: PhD student discusses with their advisor before using ChatGPT for outlining. The advisor agrees it's acceptable to use as a brainstorming tool, and the student documents this conversation.

title: Generating interview coding categories
prompt: A qualitative researcher has 50 interviews about experiences with chronic illness. They use an AI tool to help generate an initial codebook of themes before reviewing it manually and adjusting based on their data.

title: Generating interview coding categories (publicly anonymized data)
prompt: A qualitative researcher has 50 interviews about general workplace well-being, with no sensitive personal identifiers. The data is already published in an open-access archive. They use an AI tool to help generate an initial codebook of themes before reviewing it manually and adjusting based on their data.

title: Using AI to summarize key findings from interviews
prompt: After manually coding 30 interviews, a researcher uses GPT-4 to generate a concise summary of key findings. They fact-check the summary against their codes and update the publication draft accordingly.

title: Using AI to summarize findings (with disclosure)
prompt: After manually coding 30 interviews, a researcher uses GPT-4 to generate a concise summary of key findings. They fact-check the summary against their codes and update the publication draft accordingly. They include in the methods section: 'AI assistance (GPT-4) was used to generate an initial summary draft, which was then validated against coded interviews.'

title: Interpreting statistical results
prompt: A researcher runs a complex mixed-effects model and uses ChatGPT to help interpret the output tables and write up the interpretation section. They compare the AI output against academic literature before finalizing.

title: Interpreting statistical results (researcher is junior)
prompt: A first-year PhD student (new to mixed-effects models) relies heavily on ChatGPT to interpret their results. They do not independently verify the interpretations before submitting.

title: IRB study uses AI in analysis (institutional guidance exists)
prompt: A researcher with an approved IRB protocol for interviews wants to use an AI tool for thematic analysis. Their institution has published guidance on AI use in IRB-approved studies, including disclosure requirements.

title: IRB study uses AI in analysis (no guidance)
prompt: A researcher with an approved IRB protocol for interviews wants to use an AI tool for thematic analysis. Their institution has no published guidance on AI use in human subjects research. The researcher must decide on their own whether to use AI and how to disclose it.

title: AI-assisted literature search (verifying results)
prompt: A researcher uses GPT-4 with research databases to help identify papers matching their inclusion criteria. They manually verify all suggested papers and check that the AI did not miss important papers through targeted database searches.

title: AI-assisted literature search (minimal verification)
prompt: A researcher uses ChatGPT to find papers and accepts the results without systematically verifying completeness or checking that no key papers were missed.

title: Using AI to draft a peer review
prompt: A peer reviewer uses an AI tool to help structure their review of a manuscript, but does not upload the manuscript text or include confidential details in the AI prompt. They rewrite and personalize the review entirely.

title: Using AI to draft a peer review (uploading manuscript)
prompt: A peer reviewer pastes the full manuscript text into ChatGPT and asks the tool to generate a detailed review. The manuscript is confidential, and sharing it with a third-party AI system may violate ethical guidelines.

title: Using AI for student learning support (coding assignment)
prompt: A teaching assistant uses an AI tool to generate example solutions for coding assignments that students might reference, but students are required to write their own code and must demonstrate understanding in an oral exam.

title: Using AI to do student assignments (dissertation writing)
prompt: A student submits an AI-generated dissertation chapter, lightly edited, without disclosing AI use to their advisor. The chapter is passed off as primarily the student's own work.

title: Using AI for code generation (internal tool, no data)
prompt: A researcher uses GitHub Copilot to help write data processing code for an internal project. No sensitive data or proprietary algorithms are shared with the AI system.

title: Using AI for code generation (with proprietary algorithm)
prompt: A researcher shares a proprietary machine learning algorithm with ChatGPT to ask for optimization suggestions. The code represents months of development and competitive advantage.

title: AI-generated figure captions (reviewed and edited)
prompt: A researcher uses AI to generate initial figure captions for a manuscript, reviews them for accuracy against the actual figure data, and edits them as needed before publication.

title: AI-generated abstract (no fact-checking)
prompt: A researcher uses GPT to generate an abstract for a paper without carefully checking whether all claims match the paper's actual findings and data.

title: Using a public AI chatbot for participant communication
prompt: A researcher uses a ChatGPT plugin to help draft study recruitment messages to participants. The messages are reviewed and personalized before sending, and no participant data is shared with the AI system.

title: Using a public AI chatbot as a participant-facing tool
prompt: A researcher deploys ChatGPT as a direct participant-facing survey tool to answer questions about a study. Participants interact with the chatbot thinking it is a human. No disclosure occurs.

title: Training an AI model on your research data
prompt: A researcher wants to fine-tune a language model on their published dataset to improve predictions for their specific research context. The dataset contains demographic information about study participants.

title: Publishing model outputs without disclosure
prompt: A researcher generates synthetic data using a generative AI model to supplement their real experimental data in a publication. They do not disclose the use of AI in the methods section.
